title: 越…越… and 越来越
explain: 越…越… means 'the more … the more …': 他越说越快 'He speaks faster and faster'; 汉语歌越听越好听 'This song sounds better the more you listen to it'.
越来越 + adjective (or a feeling verb such as 喜欢) means 'more and more': 天气越来越冷 'The weather gets colder and colder'; 我越来越喜欢汉语了 'I like Chinese more and more'. A final 了 is common.
Both parts of 越 stand right before the words they describe. Do not add 很 after them.

examples.en: He speaks faster and faster.
Chinese songs sound better the more you listen to them.
The weather has become colder and colder.
I have come to like Chinese more and more.

mistakes: Put 越 before both words: 雨越下越大. 雨下越大 is wrong.
Do not add 很 after 越来越: say 天气越来越冷, not 天气越来越很冷.

q.en: The rain is getting heavier and heavier.
The weather gets colder and colder.
My Chinese is getting better and better.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The weather gets colder and colder?
q.en: The weather gets colder and colder.
q.explain: 越来越 comes right before the adjective.

q.en: The weather has become colder and colder.
q.explain: Do not add 很 after 越来越.

title: 才 and 就: late and early
explain: 才 after a time word means 'only then': it happened later than expected. 他八点才到学校 'He did not get to school until eight'. 我等了半个小时，他才来 'I waited half an hour before he came'.
就 after a time word means 'as early as': it happened sooner than expected. 他六点就起床了 'He got up as early as six'.
So the same time word gives opposite feelings: 他六点才起床 (late) and 他六点就起床了 (early). A 就 sentence about the past normally ends with 了; a 才 sentence does not.
才 can also mean 'only' with a small amount or a time that is not late: 这件衣服才三十块 'This piece of clothing is only thirty yuan'; 才八点，别急 'It is only eight o'clock, don't worry'.

examples.en: He did not get to school until eight.
He got up as early as six.
This piece of clothing is only thirty yuan.

examples.zh: 我等了半个小时，他才来。
examples.en: I waited half an hour before he came.

mistakes: 才 and 就 are not interchangeable. 他六点才起床 says he got up late; 他六点就起床了 says he got up early.
Use 才 for late and 就 for early, and put both before the verb: 他八点才到, 他六点就到了. A 才 sentence about the past usually has no 了 at the end.

q.en: He did not get to school until eight.
q.explain: Time + 才 + verb: later than expected.

q.en: I got up as early as six.
q.explain: Time + 就 + verb + 了: earlier than expected.

q.en: He does not get up until ten.
We arrived as early as seven.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He got up as early as five?
q.en: He got up as early as five.

title: 刚, 刚刚 and 刚才: just
explain: 刚 means 'just (a moment ago)': 我刚到家 'I have just got home'; 电影刚开始 'The film has just started'. It goes before the verb. 刚刚 is the same with more stress, 'only just': 他刚刚出去 'He has only just gone out'.
刚才 means 'just now'. It is a time word, so it can come before the subject: 刚才谁给你打电话？ 'Who called you just now?'
刚 cannot stand before the subject: say 我刚到, not 刚我到. Use 刚才 there.

examples.en: I have just finished eating.
The film has just started.
Who called you just now?
He has only just gone out.

mistakes: 刚 goes right before the verb. 刚我吃饭 is wrong; say 我刚吃饭 or 刚才我吃饭.
Do not use 刚 for the future. 我刚去 never means 'I will go'.

q.en: I have just got home.
Who called you just now?
He has just got up.
Where did you go just now?

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The film has just started?
q.en: The film has just started.
q.explain: 刚 goes right before the verb.

title: 一直, 总是, 常常 and 平时: always and often
explain: 一直 means 'all along, without stopping': 我一直在学汉语 'I have been studying Chinese all along'. With a direction it means 'straight': 一直往前走，银行就在左边 'Go straight ahead, and the bank is on the left'.
总是 (or 总) means 'always, every time': 他总是很早到学校 'He always gets to school very early'. 老 + verb is a casual way to complain: 他老迟到 'He is always late'.
常 and 常常 mean 'often': 我们常常在这儿见面 'We often meet here'. 平时 and 一般 mean 'usually': 我平时七点起床 'I usually get up at seven'.
All of these go before the verb, after the subject.

examples.en: I have been studying Chinese all along.

examples.zh: 一直往前走，银行就在左边。
examples.en: Go straight ahead, and the bank is on the left.
He always gets to school very early.
We often meet here.

mistakes: Put these words before the verb: 我一直在这里等你, not 我在这里等你一直.
总是 means every time, 常常 means many times. Do not use 总是 when it is only 'often'.

q.en: I have been waiting for you here all along.
q.explain: 一直 goes before the verb.

q.en: He is always very busy.
q.explain: 总是 goes before the verb.

q.en: Please go straight ahead.
q.explain: 一直 + direction means straight on.

q.en: We often eat together.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He is always late?
q.en: He is always late.
q.explain: 总是 goes before the verb.

title: 更, 比较, 挺, 特别 and 极了: how much
explain: These words say how much, and each one already does the job of 很. 比较 means 'fairly, rather': 这个问题比较难. 挺 means 'quite', and is often followed by 的: 他的汉语挺好的 'His Chinese is quite good'. 特别 means 'especially, very': 这里的菜特别好吃 'The food here is especially delicious'.
更 means 'even more' and is used to compare: 这个比那个更大 'This one is even bigger than that one'.
极了 goes after the adjective and means 'extremely': 今天的天气好极了 'The weather today is extremely nice'; 我累极了 'I am tired out'.
A rough scale from weak to strong: 比较, 挺, 很, 特别, 极了.

examples.en: His Chinese is quite good.
The food here is especially delicious.
The weather today is extremely nice.
This one is even bigger than that one.

mistakes: Do not add 很 to these words: 很挺好 and 很特别好 are wrong. Each one already says how much.
极了 comes after the adjective: 好极了, not 极了好.

q.en: His Chinese is quite good.
It is especially cold today.
I am extremely tired.
q.explain: 极了 comes after the adjective.

q.en: This one is even bigger than that one.
This dish is quite delicious.
q.explain: Do not add 很 to 挺.

title: 一样, 不同 and more ways to compare
explain: A 跟 B 一样 means 'A is the same as B': 我的手机跟你的一样 'My phone is the same as yours'. Add an adjective for 'as … as': 他跟我一样高 'He is as tall as me'. The negative is 不一样: 这两个字不一样 'These two characters are not the same'. 不同 means 'different' and sounds a little more formal: 两个城市的天气不同.
比 + 更 or 还 means 'even more': 今天比昨天还冷 'Today is even colder than yesterday'. Do not add 很.
比 + adjective + 多了 means 'much more': 他比我高多了 'He is much taller than me'.
跟…比起来 means 'compared with …': 跟我的手机比起来，你的手机大多了 'Compared with my phone, yours is much bigger'.

examples.en: My phone is the same as yours.
Today is even colder than yesterday.
He is much taller than me.
These two characters are not the same.

mistakes: Do not add 很 in a 比 sentence: 他比我更高 is right, 他比我很更高 is wrong.
In 跟…一样 the adjective comes after 一样: 他跟我一样高, not 他跟我高一样.

q.en: He is as tall as me.
q.explain: A + 跟 + B + 一样 + adjective.

q.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.
He is much taller than me.
q.explain: 比 + adjective + 多了 means much more.

q.en: These two characters are not the same.
q.explain: 不一样 means not the same.

q.en: He is even taller than me.
q.explain: Do not add 很 in a 比 sentence.

title: 难 and 容易: hard to, easy to
explain: 难 + verb means 'hard to …': 这种鞋很难买 'This kind of shoes is hard to buy'; 汉语不难学 'Chinese is not hard to learn'. The thing you are talking about comes first, then 难, then the verb.
容易 + verb means 'easy to …': 这个问题很容易回答 'This question is easy to answer'. It can also mean 'likely to': 冬天容易感冒 'It is easy to catch a cold in winter'.
Some of these have become words of their own: 难看 'ugly', 难听 'unpleasant to hear'. The opposite pattern with 好 is common too: 好看, 好吃, 好听.
If you want to say how hard or easy, 很 goes before 难 or 容易.

examples.en: Chinese is not hard to learn.
This question is easy to answer.
This kind of shoes is hard to buy.
It is easy to catch a cold in winter.

mistakes: Put 很 before 难 or 容易, not after: 很难写, not 难很写.
The thing you talk about usually comes first: 这个字很难写 sounds more natural than 很难写这个字.

q.en: Chinese is not hard to learn.
This question is easy to answer.
This character is hard to write.
It is easy to catch a cold in winter.
q.explain: 容易 means easy to or likely to.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Chinese songs are hard to learn?
q.en: Chinese songs are hard to learn.

title: 听得懂 and 听不懂: can or cannot
explain: Put 得 between a verb and its result to say you can reach that result, and 不 to say you cannot: 我听不懂 'I cannot understand (what I hear)'; 你看得清楚吗？ 'Can you see clearly?'
Common ones: 听得懂 / 听不懂 (understand by listening), 看得见 / 看不见 (see), 吃得完 / 吃不完 (finish eating), 找得到 / 找不到 (find), 买得到 / 买不到 (be able to buy).
In statements the 不 form is far more common: 这么多菜，我吃不完 'There is so much food that I cannot finish it'. The 得 form is mostly used in questions and answers.
Use this pattern instead of 不能 + result: say 我听不懂, not 我不能听懂.

examples.zh: 老师说得太快，我听不懂。
examples.en: The teacher speaks too fast, and I cannot understand.
Can you see clearly?
There is so much food that I cannot finish it.
I cannot find my phone.

mistakes: Do not say 我不能听懂. For 'I cannot understand' say 我听不懂.
The result comes after 得 or 不: 听不懂, not 听懂不.

q.en: I cannot understand.
Can you see clearly?
q.explain: Verb + 得 + result, then 吗.

q.en: There is so much food that I cannot finish it.
q.explain: 吃不完 means cannot finish eating.

q.en: I cannot find my phone.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I cannot hear clearly?
q.en: I cannot hear clearly.

title: 起来, 出来, 下去 and 向
explain: After a verb, direction words such as 进 'in', 出 'out' and 回 'back' go in front of 来 or 去: 他走进来了 'He has walked in', 出去 'go out', 回来 'come back'. If there is a place, it goes between the two parts: 他回学校去了 'He has gone back to school'.
起来 can mean 'start to': 他笑起来了 'He started to laugh'. 下去 can mean 'go on': 请说下去 'Please go on speaking'.
向 + direction or person means 'toward': 孩子们向老师跑去了 'The children ran toward the teacher'; 请向前走 'Please walk forward'.

examples.en: He started to laugh.
Please come in.
Please go on speaking.
The children ran toward the teacher.

mistakes: Do not put a place after 来 or 去: say 他回学校去了, not 他回去学校了.
Do not put a plain direction word like 起 on its own after a verb. It needs 来: 笑起来.

q.en: He has walked in.
He has gone back to school.
q.explain: The place goes between 回 and 去.

q.en: The children ran toward the teacher.
Please go on speaking.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He has gone back to school?
q.en: He has gone back to school.
q.explain: The place goes between 回 and 去.

title: How long: 学了两年 and 三年没见了
explain: To say how long something lasted, put the time length after the verb and 了: 我学了两年汉语 'I studied Chinese for two years'. The time length comes before the object.
Add a second 了 at the end if it is still going on: 他在这里工作了三年了 'He has worked here for three years (and still does)'.
Time length + 没 + verb + 了 means 'has not … for …': 我们三年没见面了 'We have not met for three years'.
The time length never goes before the verb: 我两年学汉语 is wrong.

examples.en: I studied Chinese for two years.

examples.zh: 他在这里工作了三年了。
examples.en: He has worked here for three years.
We have not met for three years.
He waited for you for an hour.

mistakes: Time length goes after the verb, not before: 我学了两年汉语, not 我两年学汉语.
Without the final 了 the action is finished; with it, the action is still going on.

q.en: I studied Chinese for two years.
We have not met for three years.
q.explain: Time length + 没 + verb + 了.

q.en: He waited for you for an hour.
q.explain: 了 comes right after the verb.

q.en: We have not met for three years.
q.explain: 没 + verb says it has not happened.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I studied Chinese for two years?
q.en: I studied Chinese for two years.
q.explain: The time length comes before the object.
